title: Little Knocker-Upper
subtitle: The wind, blowing through this place, has seen everything.

trails.title: That Thick, Stubborn ...
trails.description: Some liken it to pea soup, others to the famous Spartan black broth.

content.text:
- It is half past ten in the morning, yet even by the window, the page cannot be read without a lamp. I set the journal by the sill, lit the lamp, and returned to find it layered in fine coal ash.

- Best to refrain from keeping the windows open for now.

- On the Thames, visibility is so low that feeding the swans is a hopeless task. I hear their mournful calls but cannot see them. Their wings beat against the smog like warnings to retreat.

- Records suggest fogs like these are unusual for this season.

- Cases of tuberculosis are on the rise. While I have no firm statistics, the overcrowding in hospitals and sanatoriums tells its own story.

- By tea time, visibility's improved slightly. The bus lamps barely pierce the fog, their faint glow the only evidence of their passage.

- Not good. Now my chest is starting to burn too.

- At the hospital, there's talk of a "Black Fog" capable of flattening buildings. Supposedly, one hospital was claimed in such a disaster. A tiny tornado? No, didn't look like it. Either this is a macabre joke, or someone should call up an arcanist to investigate.

items.text: As morning breaks, the rooster crows, announcing the start of another day of hard labor for the people of the East End.
In this land of industry, shipyards, and factories, there is a dire need of coal, fuel, and the labor to sustain them.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Good mornin'! Sir, madam, this here is your wake-up call!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Rise and shine! Wakey time!
Flutterpage looks up to the gray sky above. There is only a touch of blue, and no sun, stars, or moon to be seen.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: Enough! I said enough with it, girl! I'm already awake, ain't I? So, stop buzzing around!
The seasoned knocker-upper deftly dodges the basin full of foot-washing water that has just been flung out the window and slips through the alley and onto the next street.
She still has a job to do.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Wakey, wakey! Morning's here!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Mrs. Wilson? You awake? You can't be late again, or old Mister Pig-Eyes will be on you with his belt!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: What happened? Didn't she hear me?
Suddenly, she's shoved from behind.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ahhh!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oi! Who did that?

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Shut up already, Liberti. Didn't you know Mrs. Wilson was sick?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: She's sick? What's wrong? It doesn't hurt like swallowin' a burnin' coal, does it?

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Who told you that?

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Yeah, maybe. Plenty of folks been gettin' that too. My dad says it's a curse!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: It's not a curse, dummy!

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: I'm no dummy, Liberti. You are! Believin' anythin' what that hag told you! She's a dirty, ugly, old liar, and she's the one who cursed everyone here!

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: She's a toad! A toad what can't get out of her house to see sunlight, and decided to curse us all just 'cause she didn't like the fair!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Have you gone off your rocker, Freddy! Just leave me alone! I got work to do.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: That's work, eh? You call knockin' on people's window work?
The boy rolls up his sleeve and pats his bicep.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: I climb up in the steam turbines to tighten up the screws, and I clean them chimneys from the inside. Think you can do that, eh?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But I don't want to tighten screws or climb up chimneys! I don't like the smells.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Oh, so you like the smell of this black fog, do you? All thanks to your wicked hag friend.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Go away!
She whips a clothesline pole at the boy's knee with a sharp crack.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Ow-ah!
The boy leaps toward the girl but loses her among the heap of rags.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Huh?
He swivels his head toward the sound and stands there shocked as Flutterpage deftly leaps over him.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: What the ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: The fog lady taught me this.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Lady? You mean that hag? I should've guessed you'd be that ugly toad witch's apprentice!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: You're not my friend anymore!
She runs off deeper into Cross Street.
Old House, Cross Street
The old mansion looks just as it always does. From the strange garden to the ominous building half lost in the haze of the smog.
Even so, Flutterpage is hit by an unusual feeling, one she can't quite place.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: It's not snail delivery day, but after she threw me out of the house last time, maybe I'll go apologize.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Maybe then I can learn some more tricks from her, or at least read her books!

items.speaker: Vines Carbuncle
items.text: Squeak?
The creature eyes her wearily.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hello, hello!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Now, why didn't you let Ms. Tooth Fairy in last time? She's not a bad person. She even gave me some flyin' medicine. It was sweet and sour.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: You think Ms. Willow's lonely? She needs new friends, and maybe some flyin' medicine too?

items.speaker: Vines Carbuncle
items.text: Squeak!
The Carbuncle seems to reject her assessment, leaping side to side in a clear display of defiance.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But this time I won't go through the window. Not that I get why she was so mad? Was it that I stopped her from eatin' breakfast maybe?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Well, time to figure it out. I bet if I walk in from the front door, she won't be so angry.
Flutterpage enters the garden like she always does, except this time, the Carbuncles don't make way for her.

items.speaker: Vines Carbuncle
items.text: *roar*
They leap at her.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: What's wrong?
Flutterpage swings the clothesline pole, but fails to drive them off. They close in on her, malice in their eyes.
Fortunately, reinforcements come galloping through the smog.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Ms. Flutterpage? What in the blazes are you doing here?! Good lord! I hope you didn't get hurt!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Mr. Hat!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Ms. Bartley, I'd advise you to please stay a safe distance back.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: No ...

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Just look at the state of this garden. Oh, Charlotte, what have you been through to fall this far?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Thank goodness, you're in one piece.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I ... I don't get it. They ain't never bit me before.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Well, you must always stay alert when you encounter critters, even in a familiar place. That's some genuine ranger's advice.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: A ranger? Are you really a ranger? Can you be a ranger without a real horse? Will I get a hat like you if I get to be a ranger?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Errrrr.
Fortunately, a hat's range of expressions doesn't include awkwardness, or much else for that matter.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hi, Miss. Are you here for the lady livin' here?
Flutterpage circles the unfamiliar lady, looking her up and down.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Miss, you look a lot like Ms. Willow—the Fog Lady. So straight and proper like a swan.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Ms. Willow, you said?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm.
Flutterpage claps her mouth before realizing she wasn't the one to utter this name.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Y-Yes, Ms. Willow. Did she say you were allowed to call her that too, Miss?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Allowed?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: *sigh*
Even her sigh carries an elegant, melodious quality.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: What kind of nutter has she become?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Thank you for taking me here, Mr. Brimley. I can handle the rest myself.
She makes a gentle motion with her hand, signaling that she has finished talking.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: You're welcome. Let's go shall we, eh little tacker? It's not safe to leave you here.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: I'll escort you to the hospital. Ms. Tooth Fairy needs your help.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Alright.
Flutterpage holds onto Brimley's coat as the two of them leave the garden. She looks back a few times. Caroline remains totally unmoving.
It's as though she can converse with the owner of the house through her stare alone.
Temporary Hospital

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I thought a hospital was a big, big buildin'! This is more like a fair, only with sick people.
Patients lie on basic steel-frame beds, their once-pristine white sheets now marked with yellow and gray stains.
In the face of such a scene, the bright flags of the Uluru Games now look lifeless and limp.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Well, you're right there, mate. It's not your typical hospital. Arthur's calling it the "London Emergency Relief Centre for Special Tuberculosis Patients."

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But it's still kind of a hospital, ain't it?
She doesn't linger on this thought for long. The image of the unfamiliar lady in Willow's garden won't leave her mind.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Who's that Swan lady? She's not from Cross Street. How did she know Ms. Wi-Fog Lady?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Swan? I suppose you mean Ms. Caroline Bartley. We're hoping she'll be our lifesaver.
Mr. Fog appears behind them, looking rather pale.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Lifesaver?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Exactly so.
There's a curious spark behind Mr. Fog's eyes. He looks straight ahead as he speaks.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: See, my hat friend, we civil servants can actually accomplish a thing or two!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: We found Ms. Bartley, a shining star of Uluru, a talented competitor! And above all, she's an insider.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: She arrived in London days ago, looking for our Fog Lady. She claimed to be an old acquaintance. Some luck, isn't it?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: If she can figure out the connection between her, the black fog, and this fiery TB—Oh! Speaking of which, that "Ms. Willow" truly has a ... special name. Heh heh.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Heh heh? What are you laughing at? How long have you been up, mate?
A thought crosses Brimley's "mind." His partner has probably hardly slept all week.
A burst of glorious vigor illuminates the Fogwalker's face, like sunlight breaking through a gap in the gray sky.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Sleep? Who needs to sleep at a time like this? I'm more than energetic. I'm a veritable locomotive, better than ever!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Arthur, you need to get some shut-eye, mate.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Is that what you think? That I'll just go back home for a little rest now? Now of all times? Dead wrong, mate. We've got rounds to make at the London Emergency Relief Centre for Special Tuberculosis Patients.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Come with me, my chapeau chap! We've got a city to save!
Mr. Fog grabs the hobbyhorse and forcibly drags Brimley away with him.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Oh, alright. Ms. Flutterpage, go find Ms. Tooth Fairy, would you? She said your arcane skill might be of some help!
The two of them quickly vanish into the streets.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: My arcane skill?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Help? How can I help a witch doctor? Maybe Ms. Tooth Fairy will tell me. But where is she?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: So many people here. I can hardly tell them from one another. Oh, but she has got those golden fairies with her. Maybe I can "see" them.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Like how Ms. Willow taught me.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: To control the wind, you need to learn to see it first.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Can you see the wind, lass?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Only when it's blowin' somethin' around, like dust or old paper.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But I ain't got nothin' like that with me now. I used all of it when Freddy tried to catch me. Is there anythin' else I can use?
She scans through the pale yellow smog, the fluttering Uluru flags informing her of the wind's direction.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh, I see it!
The wind picks up, and the flags, along with the people's clothes, start to flutter in the same direction.

items.speaker: Patient I
items.text: What with this wind, eh? Where's it coming from? Oi! My hat!

items.speaker: Patient II
items.text: *cough* Please, is there any good Samaritan who can spare a blanket? Oh, God bless you!
The smog dissipates in the wind, and for a brief moment, the air is noticeably clearer in this small corner of the world.
At one of the beds, a little golden fairy is being held by its wings and placed into a patient's mouth.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy!

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Flutterpage, there you are.
She swiftly closes the patient's mouth, making him swallow her bizarre medicine before walking briskly over to Flutterpage.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: What's wrong?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: We've got to find a way to clear up the sky!
